→ Supply chain security now requires anti-bot measures at the e-commerce layer
→ The same proxy/rotation tech used for web scraping is being weaponized for hardware hoarding

The irony: the companies building anti-bot solutions are watching bots take over a new vertical every quarter.

Sneakers → GPUs → DRAM → what's next?

#BotDetection #SupplyChain #DataInfrastructure

title: All it takes to poison AI training data is to create a website
summary: Article URL: https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2026/02/poisoning-ai-training-data.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47209286 Points: 5 # Comments: 2
override_reason: AI data poisoning via websites — web scraping meets AI safety
post_en:
All it takes to poison an AI model is a website.

Researchers just demonstrated that creating a single website with manipulated content can inject false information into AI training datasets.

The implications:
→ Web scraping pipelines lack adversarial data validation
→ Any website could become a vector for training data manipulation
→ The "garbage in, garbage out" problem has a new, deliberate dimension

This is the dark side of the open web as a training corpus. If you can't verify the source, you can't trust the model.

Data infrastructure teams need to think about provenance, not just volume.

→ Пайплайны веб-скрейпинга не имеют валидации на adversarial-данные
→ Любой сайт может стать вектором для манипуляции обучающими данными

title: Stolen Gemini API key racks up $82,000 in 48 hours
summary: Article URL: https://llmhorrors.com/all/gemini-stolen-api-key-82k/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47231469 Points: 37 # Comments: 17
override_reason: API key theft + $82K loss — security, automation, credential abuse
post_en:
$82,000 burned through a stolen API key in 48 hours.

A developer's Gemini API key was compromised. Within two days, someone racked up eighty-two thousand dollars in usage.

The pattern is becoming alarmingly common:
→ API keys leaked in public repos or logs
→ Automated systems exploit them within minutes
→ Cloud bills balloon before anyone notices

3 lessons from this $82K mistake:
1. Rotate API keys like passwords — regularly, not "someday"
2. Set hard spending caps, not just alerts
3. Monitor usage patterns, not just total spend

In the API economy, a single credential leak is now a five-figure problem.

#APISecurity #CloudInfrastructure #DataSecurity

Паттерн становится пугающе частым:
→ API-ключи утекают через публичные репозитории или логи
→ Автоматизированные системы эксплуатируют их за минуты
→ Счета за облако раздуваются быстрее, чем кто-то замечает

3 урока из этой ошибки на $82K:
1. Ротируйте API-ключи как пароли — регулярно, а не "когда-нибудь"
2. Ставьте жёсткие лимиты расходов, а не просто алерты
3. Мониторьте паттерны использования, а не только общую сумму

В API-экономике одна утечка ключа — это уже пятизначная проблема.

title: EFF to Court: Don’t Make Embedding Illegal
summary: Who should be directly liable for online infringement – the entity that serves it up or a user who embeds a link to it? For almost two decades, most U.S. courts have held that the former is responsible, applying a rule called the server test. Under the server test, whomever controls the server that hosts a copyrighted work—and therefore determines who has access to what and how—can be directly liable if that content turns out to be infringing. Anyone else who merely links to it can be secondarily liable in some circumstances (for example, if that third party promotes the infringement), but isn’t on the hook under most circumstances. The test just makes sense. In the analog world, a person is free to tell others where they may view a third party’s display of a copyrighted work, without being directly liable for infringement if that display turns out to be unlawful. The server test is the straightforward application of the same principle in the online context. A user that links to a picture, video, or article isn’t in charge of transmitting that content to the world, nor are they in a good position to know whether that content violates copyright. In fact, the user doesn’t even control what’s located on the other end of the link—the person that controls the server can change what’s on it at any time, such as swapping in different images, re-editing a video or rewriting an article. But a news publisher, Emmerich Newspapers, wants the Fifth Circuit to reject the server test, argui
override_reason: EFF legal defense of embedding — scraping/fair use precedent
post_en:
The EFF just told a court: making embedding illegal would break the internet.

Embedding — linking to content hosted elsewhere — is the foundation of how the web works.

If courts rule that embedding = copying:
→ Every website that embeds a tweet, image, or video becomes liable
→ Search engines, news aggregators, and social platforms face existential risk
→ Web scraping and data collection case law gets rewritten overnight

The EFF's argument: embedding isn't reproduction. It's pointing.

This case matters for everyone in data infrastructure. The legal framework for how data moves across the web is being decided right now.

#DataLaw #FairUse #WebInfrastructure
post_ru:
EFF заявила суду: запрет embedding сломает интернет.

Embedding — ссылка на контент, размещённый в другом месте — это основа работы веба.

Если суды решат, что embedding = копирование:
→ Каждый сайт, встраивающий твит, картинку или видео, станет ответчиком
→ Поисковики, агрегаторы и соцсети получат экзистенциальный риск
→ Прецедентное право по web scraping и data collection перепишут за ночь

Аргумент EFF: embedding — это не копирование. Это указание.

Это дело важно для всех в data infrastructure. Правовую рамку для движения данных по вебу решают прямо сейчас.

#DataLaw #FairUse #WebInfrastructure

title: AI’s Silent Killer – Toxic Data
summary: AI’s Silent Killer – Toxic Data    The AI Journal
override_reason: Data quality crisis for AI — data infrastructure insider angle
post_en:
AI's silent killer isn't compute costs. It's toxic data.

Everyone talks about GPU shortages and model architecture. Almost nobody talks about what happens when your training data is poisoned.

The quiet crisis:
→ Biased datasets produce biased models at scale
→ Synthetic data loops amplify errors exponentially  
→ Most companies have no data quality pipeline — just data volume targets

The companies winning the AI race aren't the ones with the most data. They're the ones with the cleanest data.

Data quality > Data quantity. Every time.

#AITraining #DataQuality #DataInfrastructure

→ Петли синтетических данных усиливают ошибки экспоненциально

Компании, выигрывающие гонку AI — не те, у кого больше данных. А те, у кого самые чистые данные.

title: Wikipedia vs Grokipedia: 5x the Pages, 70x the Citations, 1615x the Traffic
summary: Is Grokipedia a serious competitor to Wikipedia, or just a doomed exercise in billionaire hubris? Does Grok bring new value to the table, or just rehash the same old content? Does Grokipedia influence AI search in a similar way to … Read more ›
override_reason: Wikipedia vs Grokipedia — AI-generated content battle, great data
post_en:
Wikipedia: 5x the pages. 70x the citations. 1,615x the traffic.

Grokipedia tried to replace Wikipedia with AI-generated content. The numbers are brutal:
→ 1,615x less traffic
→ 70x fewer citations from credible sources
→ AI-generated doesn't mean AI-trusted

The lesson for anyone building with AI content: volume without authority is noise.

Wikipedia's moat isn't technology. It's 20+ years of community-verified trust.

You can generate a million pages overnight. You can't generate credibility.

#AIContent #DataQuality #ContentStrategy
post_ru:

Grokipedia попыталась заменить Wikipedia AI-контентом. Цифры жестокие:
→ В 1 615 раз меньше трафика
→ В 70 раз меньше цитирований из авторитетных источников
→ AI-generated не значит AI-trusted

Урок для всех, кто строит на AI-контенте: объём без авторитета — это шум.

Рубеж Wikipedia — не технология. Это 20+ лет верифицированного сообществом доверия.

Можно сгенерировать миллион страниц за ночь. Нельзя сгенерировать авторитет.

title: Show HN: ClawShield – Open-source security proxy for AI agents (Go, eBPF)
summary: Author here. ClawShield is a security proxy that sits in front of OpenClaw (open-source AI gateway) and scans all inbound/outbound messages. The core is an HTTP/WebSocket reverse proxy in Go (~6k lines) with four scanners: 1. Prompt injection detection - three tiers: regex heuristics (role overrides, instruction injection, delimiter attacks, encoding attacks), structural analysis (base64-decoded instruction blocks, imperative verb density scoring), and canary token leak detection. 2. Secrets/PII scanning - regex argument filters applied to decoded JSON values (defeats unicode escape bypasses like \u0070assword). 3. Vulnerability scanning - SQLi (UNION, tautologies, blind with SLEEP/BENCHMARK), SSRF (private IPs, cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, decimal/hex IP encoding, dangerous schemes like gopher://), path traversal (double URL-encoding, null bytes), command injection (shell metacharacters, backtick execution), XSS. 4. Malware detection - magic bytes for PE/ELF/Mach-O, YARA-like signature rules for reverse shells and C2 frameworks, archive bomb detection via compression ratio, Shannon entropy analysis. Policy engine is deny-by-default YAML. You define tool allowlists, denylists, per-tool argument filters, domain allowlists, and per-agent/per-channel restrictions. Every decision is logged to SQLite. title: Show HN: Proxelar – MitM proxy with (rata)TUI, terminal, and web interface
summary: I built this over the past couple of years as a way to inspect HTTP/HTTPS traffic (learning project). It started as a Tauri desktop app but I recently simplified the whole thing — dropped the desktop GUI and replaced it with three simpler interfaces (TUI with ratatui https://github.com/ratatui/ratatui, terminal, web) that you pick with a CLI flag. The proxy intercepts both HTTP and HTTPS, works as a forward or reverse proxy, and lets you search and drill into individual request/response pairs. The TUI is the default — it gives you a live table of traffic with detail panels. The web interface streams everything over WebSocket if you prefer a browser. Terminal mode just prints colored lines, useful for piping or logging. Setup is pretty minimal — install, run, point your system proxy at it. Happy to hear feedback or ideas. Still a lot I want to improve. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47220224 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
